history.dynasty: Origins traced to the 14th century (sung by poet-saint Arunagirinathar); modern temple built from 1968 by Balamurugan Adimai Swamy, with renovations in 1980 and 2001
history.period: 14th century (ancient shrine); present stone temple from 1968 onwards
history.summary: This is the famous Rathnagiri Balamurugan Temple on the Ratnagiri hillock at Walajah, on the Chennai-Bangalore Highway about 14-17 km from Vellore - matching the brief's identification of the famous 'Balamurugan Temple [Vellore]'. The shrine traces to the 14th century and was sung by the poet-saint Arunagirinathar as 'Rathinagiri Vazh Murugane' (Murugan, the god of the devas, resides in Rathinagiri); it is counted among the 'Kundruthoradal' hill shrines of Murugan. Originally a small sand structure, it was transformed into a grand stone temple by Balamurugan Adimai Swamy (Thavatiru Balamurugan Adimai) starting in 1968, with major renovations in 1980 and 2001. The idol of Bala Murugan was installed in a granite chariot. A notable feature is that the temple's poojas are conducted in Tamil rather than Sanskrit. Legend holds that Indra was hidden here as a peacock by Murugan to escape a demon, and devotees believe milk offered to the deity turns into curd. CSV CORRECTION: the CSV lists district 'Vellore', but the temple stands at Wallajah in RANIPET district (Ranipet was carved out of Vellore in 2019) - district recorded as Ranipet with town 'Ratnagiri (Walajah)'. Note: one popular source claims the 14th-century construction was by Arunagirinathar himself; the majority of sources say he sang about it rather than built it - flagged.

name: Arulmigu Balamurugan Temple
town_description: Ratnagiri is a hillock at Walajah in Ranipet district, on the Vellore-Chennai highway about 14-17 km from Vellore. The temple is reached by climbing about 150 steps, with a towering gopuram, a hexagon-shaped temple pond (theppakulam) and views over the surrounding countryside; poojas are conducted in Tamil.
